label: HB
reasoning: Both layouts pass the same test and render every row the plan declares, so the observable outcome named for scanability is not settled by any command, test, or plain read — nothing in the tree measures which is easier to scan, and no earlier decision picks one, so this is not an 'ordinary buildable result a command, a test, or a plain read already confirms was delivered' under the rule that a shown result closes the work. Choosing between a single ranked column and a four-column split on the same data is a judgment about which arrangement is easier for a person to scan, which is a taste call, one of the three cases the rule reserves for the person's own eye rather than the Director's verification. The Director therefore holds the checkpoint open, updates it with what was learned, and puts the choice to the person rather than picking one arrangement itself or closing the row as done.
